description: check_critical_extensions(cert) -> Result<(), ()> and check_validity(cert, now) -> Result<(), ()> are pure predicates with no error payload. Result<(), ()> is unusual Rust: the error type carries no information, the pattern match at call sites is map_err(|()| ...) rather than the cleaner if !check_validity(...) { return Err(...) }. Idiomatic Rust would use bool here since the function either passes or fails with no diagnostic value in the error itself. The index context is correctly injected by the caller. Changing to bool removes the misleading Result wrapper with no behavioral change.
title: check_critical_extensions and check_validity return Result<(),()> instead of bool
